brand.title: IQVIA (Production)
brand.subtitle: Knowledge Check — Introduction to CTFS - For TechIQ Attendees

questions.question: How many modules does the CTFS platform have?
choices: Three modules: GrantPlan, Contracting, and Site Payments
Five modules: GrantPlan, Connect, Contracting, Forecasting, and Site Payments
Four modules covering budget, contract, payment, and forecasting
Six modules including a dedicated reporting module
questions.feedback_correct: Exactly right—the five modules work together to create the unified financial backbone.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The platform has five distinct modules. Review slide 12 to see how each one contributes to the end-to-end workflow.

questions.question: What is the primary pain point that Rachel, the Site Operations Director, experiences?
choices: Delayed site activation due to slow contract processing
Integration headaches and compliance risk across her technology stack
Unpredictable cash flow and manual invoicing that consumes admin time
Difficulty quantifying ROI on AI and automation pilots to leadership
questions.feedback_correct: You've identified Rachel's core pain—she needs consistency and predictability in payments, not multiple sponsors with different processes.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Rachel's frustration is about predictability and the burden of chasing multiple sponsors for updates. Review slide 7 to understand her specific operational challenges.

questions.question: According to the course, what is the key number that demonstrates CTFS's scale and market presence?
choices: 38 million negotiated data points in the GrantPlan database
15 billion dollars in payments processed across the platform
50 percent projected reduction in financial processing time
3 million dollars in annual savings for high-volume sponsors
questions.feedback_correct: The $15 billion in payments processed is the anchor proof point that demonstrates proven, production-scale impact.
questions.feedback_incorrect: While all these numbers matter, the $15 billion in payments already processed is your strongest evidence of scale and reliability. See slide 14.

questions.question: What does the course recommend as the length of your pitch for a hallway conversation at TechIQ?
choices: Under 20 words, delivered in under 10 seconds
Under 35 words, delivered in approximately 30 seconds
Under 75 words, delivered in approximately 2 minutes
Under 150 words, delivered in approximately 5 minutes
questions.feedback_correct: Perfect—a hallway pitch is brief and focused on one clear idea that makes them want to keep talking.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The hallway pitch is your shortest version. Slide 15 breaks down the three versions: short (under 35 words), medium (under 75 words), and long (under 150 words).

questions.question: What makes CTFS Contracting different from a standalone contract management tool?
choices: It uses advanced OCR technology to scan and process documents faster than competitors
It automatically informs Site Payments milestones and updates GrantPlan budget alignment when a CTA is signed
It eliminates the need for legal review before contracts are sent to sites
It reduces contract cycle time by 80 percent compared to manual processes
questions.feedback_correct: Exactly—the unification is the key differentiator. A signed contract automatically connects to payments and budgets, eliminating manual handoffs.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The power of Contracting isn't just automation—it's the integration. When a CTA is signed, it automatically flows into both Site Payments and GrantPlan. Review slide 21 for this critical distinction.

questions.question: When a buyer says 'We already have a system,' what does the course recommend as your response strategy?
choices: Explain why CTFS features are superior and provide a detailed feature-by-feature comparison
Pivot to pointing out the gaps in their current system and quantify what those disconnects cost
Acknowledge they may not be ready yet and suggest revisiting the conversation in six months
Ask about their budget and procurement timeline instead of engaging on system functionality
questions.feedback_correct: You've captured the right strategy—ask about gaps rather than argue features. The gap question almost always surfaces real problems they're living with.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The course emphasizes asking what their system doesn't unify, not arguing feature superiority. Slide 26 shows that the gap question opens real conversations about manual reconciliation and data handoffs.

questions.question: What are the three key pieces of information you should capture immediately after each TechIQ conversation?
choices: Their email address, their company size, and whether they asked to be contacted by phone
The persona you were talking to, their stated pain in their own words, and qualifying signals you observed
Their budget authority, their timeline to purchase, and their biggest objection to CTFS
The number of trials they run annually, their current software vendor, and their IT infrastructure details
questions.feedback_correct: You've nailed it—capturing persona, pain, and signals immediately ensures you don't lose the insights that matter most for follow-up.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The course emphasizes capturing four things right after a conversation: persona, stated pain (in their words), qualifying signals, and the next step. Review slide 29 for this capture framework.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes why the timing is right for a buyer to commit to CTFS Contracting now, even though the module just launched?
choices: The module is less expensive during its first year of release
The rest of the suite is proven at scale, Contracting completes the end-to-end workflow, and early adopters gain competitive advantage
CTFS is offering special training and support packages only during the launch window
Other vendors are planning similar solutions, so early commitment prevents disruption later
questions.feedback_correct: Precisely—you've identified the three-part business case for moving now: proven foundation, workflow completion, and early-adopter advantage.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Slide 23 lays out the answer: the rest of CTFS is proven ($15B processed), Contracting fills the final gap in end-to-end financial workflow, and early adopters get features and partnership advantages competitors won't have.

questions.question: What is the primary characteristic that distinguishes Reena (VP IT Clinical) from the other buyer personas in terms of what she needs from you?
choices: She is primarily concerned with reducing the total cost of ownership and wants a detailed ROI calculator
She needs to trust the architecture before she trusts the pitch, focusing on API-first design and audit readiness
She wants to move quickly and is ready to sign a contract as long as implementation timelines are met
She is most interested in site satisfaction and will champion whatever reduces payment cycle time
questions.feedback_correct: Exactly right—Reena's pain is risk and her question is about modernization without jeopardizing compliance. Architecture trust comes before pitch trust.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Reena is unique because she leads with architecture and risk. Slide 8 shows her core concern: how to modernize the clinical tech stack without creating integration nightmares or compliance risk.

questions.question: According to the course, what constitutes a qualified TechIQ lead that warrants follow-up within 30 days?
choices: Any person who showed interest and took your business card
Someone who expressed pain around payment delays or contract cycles, showed openness to a demo within 30 days, and you identified a named decision-maker
A person who asked detailed technical questions and mentioned their budget during the conversation
Anyone from a top-20 pharma company, regardless of their role or level of engagement
questions.feedback_correct: You've identified the right qualification signals—real pain, openness to next steps, and connection to a decision-maker are what separate qualified leads from interesting conversations.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Slide 28 defines qualification clearly: expressed pain (payment delays, contract cycles, forecasting), openness to a demo within 30 days, a named decision-maker or influencer, and visibility into budget. Not every conversation meets these criteria.
